label: Zyxel GS2220-10
description: Zyxel GS2220-10 - 8x 10/100/1000BASE-T RJ-45 plus 2x GbE combo ports (RJ-45 or SFP), L2+ managed NebulaFlex Pro switch, 20 Gbps switching capacity, 15 Mpps, fanless, no PoE.

fabric.note: Zyxel quotes 20 Gbps switching capacity and 15 Mpps forwarding rate for the GS2220-10, with a 1.5 MB packet buffer, 16 K MAC address table, 9 K jumbo frames and 32 MB flash / 256 MB RAM (datasheet Performance table, https://static.us.zyxel.com/pdf/2024/switch/ds_GS2220-10HP.pdf; the product specification table carries the same figures, https://www.zyxel.com/us/en-us/products/switch/gs2220-series/specifications). The switching capacity is the full-duplex aggregate of the port rates - 40 ports at 1G - so it caps nothing the ports cannot already do.

notes: Census from the GS2220 Series datasheet (04/23, https://static.us.zyxel.com/pdf/2024/switch/ds_GS2220-10HP.pdf) and the product specification table (https://www.zyxel.com/us/en-us/products/switch/gs2220-series/specifications). Non-PoE member: every PoE cell in the datasheet table is "-", so no PSE capability and no budget are modelled. Fanless - the datasheet Fanless row says Yes and acoustic noise is 0 dBA. Wall-mount and rack-mount kits are both in the box; 100-240 V AC fixed input, 11 W with every port loaded, 8.42 W idle. The two GbE combo ports are one cage each with both halves modelled (port9/port9-sfp, port10/port10-sfp), so an RJ45 plug or an SFP module can be cabled but never both - the engine refuses the second half with E_COMBO_OCCUPIED. The user guide notes that in a combo pair the fibre side takes priority when both are physically connected. Numbering: the datasheet numbers no ports, so ports are numbered left to right in its order (8 copper, then 2 combo); the counts are cited, the numbers are that order. The datasheet row reads "100/1000 Mbps 8" while the product page reads "10M/100M/1G (RJ-45)" and the user guide calls them 10/100/1000 Mbps ports; 10 Mbps is modelled on the two sources that state it. Firmware: the series spans two documentation trains. The GS2220-10 User's Guide is Version 4.70 Edition 3 (12/2021, https://download.zyxel.com/GS2220-10/user_guide/GS2220-10_V4.70_Ed3.pdf) and the GS2220-28HP guide is Version 5.00 Edition 1 (12/2024, https://download.zyxel.com/GS2220-28HP/user_guide/GS2220-28HP_V5.00_Ed1.pdf). The 4.70 guide calls the RS-232 port "for troubleshooting only" and names the default management address http://192.168.1.1 with admin/1234; the 5.00 guide opens the same port as the CLI door and moves the default management address to https://setup.zyxel (https, not http) with the same admin/1234 or a local credential in cloud mode. The datasheet (04/23) lists features marked "New for V4.80" (new Web interface, Flex link, auto configuration recovery, intuitive cloud connection status), so the datasheet describes a firmware newer than the 4.70 guide and older than the 5.00 one. Console parameters do not change across the two guides: 115200 bps, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit, no flow control, VT100 emulation, male 9-pin RS-232 cable. The 4.70 guide restricts that port to troubleshooting, while the datasheet feature list offers "Management through Web interface, Console, Telnet, SNMP" and a "Cisco-like CLI" - which is why cli is modelled: telnet, SSH, web and (from firmware 5.00) console all carry it.
